e1_must_have_correlation.marginal_value_statement: must_have_coverage alone has strong Spearman correlation (0.3567) with weak labels. The 12-feature monotonic XGBoost model delivers a marginal gain of +0.0725 NDCG@10 and +0.0897 Spearman Rho over must_have_coverage alone by accounting for seniority gaps, years experience, education match, and dense semantic similarity.

section_e_scoring_validity.e3_target_disclosure: Note: Precision (>85%) and ECE (<0.05) targets were self-set engineering objectives, not external standard benchmarks.

section_e4_end_to_end_200_benchmark.latency_explanation: Median run of 3 consecutive executions of the full 200-resume pipeline with 2-worker parsing pool, SHA256 parse caching, and streamed batch embedding (batch_size=24). Both wall time (125.04s <= 300s) and peak RSS (349.3 MB <= 400 MB) pass the required bars.

before_fixes.years_gap_impact: Dates polluted by trailing text or school years, causing negative years_gap calculation anomalies
before_fixes.title_match_impact: Keyword columns and placeholder strings treated as job titles, producing false matches

after_fixes.years_gap_impact: Regex strictly enforces YYYY or MM/YYYY boundaries; years_gap capped between -10.0 and +15.0 years
after_fixes.title_match_impact: Placeholders (Company Name, City, State) sanitized and skills headers excluded from titles

section_f1_vocabulary_mismatch.conclusion: Exact keyword matching fails on Candidate A (missing K8s/Postgres) and Candidate B (0 matches). The combination of canonical taxonomy alias resolution (mapping K8s -> Kubernetes, Postgres -> PostgreSQL) and dense semantic similarity (0.6865 for A, 0.5842 for B vs 0.2104 for C) successfully bridges the vocabulary mismatch gap.
